fields.description:
Objective

Confirm that the Study Link Click intake integration provides enough information (e.g. a rep identifier) to automatically resolve the correct Deal-Rep Assignment on each incoming click, and confirm whether the integration point needs to be updated to call the new Sign-Up intake path (replacing an earlier Lead-based call).

Why This Matters

The production Study Link Click resolution flow (BUILD-04) assumes this data is present. If it isn't, a refactor of the intake integration will be needed before Phase 1 go-live.

Action Needed

Confirm current API payload fields with the integration owner and align on any changes required.

fields.summary: DECISION-01 — Confirm Sign-Up Intake Integration Supports Rep Assignment Resolution

comments.body:
LIKELY RESOLVED — 2026-07-28 reconciliation.

The 2026-07-20 Deal Rep Assignment architecture decision appears to answer this: Salesforce replaces Airtable as the system of record for rep assignment, with one active state per Deal and the Deal / Deal Rep Assignment split. Rep assignment resolution in the intake flow is specified in BUILD-04 (match Rep External Id + Deal External Id where Assignment Status = Active).

ACTION: confirm this against the 2026-07-20 decision and close, rather than leaving it in Triage. If there is a residual gap, restate it as a specific question — the current title is too broad to action.

**⚠️ REOPENED 2026-08-04 — this decision is NOT settled. Do not build against either model yet.**

**Jul 28 position (Joyce):** the CMS owns rep assignment; Salesforce is a display layer.

Waleed: "you're saying, Joyce, that we're not going to click manage rep assignment in Salesforce. It's just going to display what assignments you've made in the CMS." Joyce: "Correct." \[50:56\]

**Aug 4 position (Emily):** the opposite.

Emily \[12:41\]: "I thought we moved to like, we're actually like assigning at a rep level into the CMS, into Salesforce."

Emily \[17:03\]: "we just have to rethink the UI then, I guess, like because we're talking about basically just bringing the rep assignments back into Salesforce." Joyce: "Like there's no change there then."

Kobi restated the CMS-owned model at \[18:28\] and **Joyce did not confirm** — she deferred: "I just need to not confirm right now. I think I need to have a separate discussion."

**Cost of getting this wrong is already proven.** The Salesforce Manage Rep Assignment feature was demoed and accepted on Jul 28 at \[41:13\], then rendered display-only ten minutes later at \[50:56\]. That build is sunk. BUILD-120's mockup bakes in the read-only/CMS-owned treatment again.

**Blocks:** BUILD-46 · BUILD-66 · BUILD-79 · BUILD-120 (DRA related list) · Epic WAGR-176.

**Next action:** get Joyce's "separate discussion" scheduled and a written answer to one question — _which system is the system of record for a Deal Rep Assignment?_ Everything else follows from that.
